chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Jumhūr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd al-Muʾmin, from Sālim, who said:
I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:

Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those whom We chose from among Our servants; so among them is one who wrongs his own self, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds, by the permission of Allah.
He عليه السلام said: "The one foremost in good deeds is the Imam, the moderate one is the one who recognizes the Imam, and the one who wrongs his own self is the one who does not recognize the Imam."

key_terms.اصْطَفَيْنَا: We chose; denotes divine selection and election
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the divinely appointed Imam, identified as the highest category in the verse
key_terms.الْعَارِفُ: the recognizer, meaning one who knows and acknowledges the Imam
key_terms.الْكِتَابَ: the Book, meaning the divine scripture inherited by those chosen servants
key_terms.سَابِقٌ بِالْخَيْرَاتِ: foremost in good deeds; interpreted here as the Imam
key_terms.ظَالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ: one who wrongs his own self; interpreted here as one who does not recognize the Imam
key_terms.مُقْتَصِدٌ: moderate; interpreted here as one who recognizes the Imam

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام explain the verse about those who inherit the Book in Qur'an 35:32?
ai.summary: This hadith presents an interpretation of the verse by identifying its three categories in relation to the Imam. The foremost in good deeds is the Imam, the moderate one is the one who recognizes the Imam, and the one who wrongs himself is the one who does not recognize the Imam. The narration highlights the centrality of Imamate in understanding divine guidance and the inheritance of the Book.
